validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, built, FERC-jurisdictional interstate natural gas pipeline, confirmed by 5+ independent origins: Tallgrass Energy's own in-service press release (Business Wire, June 26, 2020, via Wayback -- live URL 403s to scripted clients but is not a confirmed dead link), NS Energy/GlobalData's project profile (published May 17 2020, updated Aug 2022), Hellenic Shipping News trade coverage (Aug 23 2019, pre-completion), Pipeline News' Oct 2018 'Planned Projects' roundup (earliest capture, project already had a FERC application on file under Tallgrass Energy LP), offshore-technology.com/GlobalData's market-data profile, and EIA's official 'Historical Natural Gas Pipeline Projects (1996-2024)' dataset, which carries the exact FERC docket (CP18-102), a 'Completed' status, and matching specs. Phillips 66's FY2023 and FY2024 10-K Exhibit 21 subsidiary lists both still carry 'DCP Cheyenne Connector, LLC' as an active subsidiary, independent confirmation the asset remains in the corporate structure through Dec 31, 2024. CLASSIFICATION: correctly an interstate gas TRANSMISSION connector (not gathering) -- EIA classifies it 'Interstate,' regulator 'FERC'; it moves D-J Basin gas from receipt interconnects at processing-plant tailgates to the REX Cheyenne Hub for onward transmission, the textbook definition of a connector/lateral transmission line, not a field-gathering system. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row roster. The only name-collision risk is P0166 Cheyenne Plains Gas Pipeline (same 'Cheyenne' hub, same state, similar era) -- but P0166 is Kinder Morgan's separate CO-to-Kansas mainline from a wholly different original build (2004 FERC EIS, CP03-302) with no ownership, geometry or docket overlap with Cheyenne Connector's 2018-2020 build (CP18-102, Tallgrass/DCP). No duplicate.

contested.Owner2: DCP Midstream, LLC -- direct 50% stake unchanged, but DCP Midstream, LP became a wholly owned Phillips 66 subsidiary in Aug. 2023 (Phillips 66 completed its buy-in of all outstanding public DCP units); Phillips 66's FY2023 and FY2024 10-K Exhibit 21 subsidiary lists both name 'DCP Cheyenne Connector, LLC' (Delaware) as a Phillips 66 subsidiary, which is almost certainly the SPV that HOLDS the 50% JV interest in this pipeline on DCP's behalf

validity.researcher_notes: Batch brief flagged this exact question: 'DCP Midstream was taken fully private by Phillips 66 in 2023. Check whether the 50% moved and to whom.' Businesswire's 2020 in-service release itself explains the PRE-2023 chain: 'The owner of DCP's general partner is a joint venture between Enbridge and Phillips 66.' That JV/public-partnership structure ended in Aug. 2023 when Phillips 66 acquired all outstanding common units of DCP Midstream, LP it did not already own, making DCP wholly Phillips 66's. I checked whether the Cheyenne Connector 50% interest moved to a directly-named Phillips 66 entity or stayed inside a DCP-branded subsidiary: Phillips 66's SEC 10-K Exhibit 21 (subsidiary listings) for BOTH fiscal year-end 2023 (filed 2024-02-21) and fiscal year-end 2024 (filed 2025-02-21) list 'DCP Cheyenne Connector, LLC,' incorporated Delaware, as a Phillips 66 subsidiary -- i.e. the entity that holds DCP's 50% JV stake in this pipeline is now, and was already at 2023 year-end, wholly owned by Phillips 66 rather than by the old Enbridge/Phillips-66 JV plus public DCP unitholders. The DIRECT owner name 'DCP Midstream, LLC' is therefore still defensible as the proximate JV partner, but its ultimate corporate parent changed materially and the tracker carries no note of it. I could not find (SEC full-text search, Bing, and the harvested wiki citation pool all checked) any source stating Phillips 66 itself, rather than a DCP-branded subsidiary, was substituted as the DIRECT 50% owner on this specific JV -- so I am not proposing a straight Owner2 rename to 'Phillips 66,' only flagging the parent-company change for a researcher decision (same posture the SOP asks for on a 'deliberate GEM divergence': flag, don't overwrite).
